newsitem.title: CANADA: CBRS lowers Alcan outlook to stable.
newsitem.headline: CBRS lowers Alcan outlook to stable.

text.p: Canadian Bond Rating Service said on Wednesday it affirmed its credit ratings for Alcan Aluminium Ltd, but lowered its rating outlook to stable from positive.

CBRS said the rating outlook was revised to stable as primary aluminum prices are approaching the level reached in 1994, the lowest in many years, while margins on fabricated products are unlikely to recover in the near term.
CBRS maintained Alcan's credit ratings at A-1 for its commercial paper, A(Low) for its long term debt, and P-2(Low) for its preferred shares.
Alcan's strong financial profile should enable it to adequately finance its operations and any future expansions without any discernible impact on the credit quality, the rating agency said.
CBRS's rating applies to about $1.7 billion of total debt and $203 million of preferred shares outstanding, it said.

While the strengthening demand for aluminum in global markets has vastly improved the business positioning of Alcan, the major focus has been toward debt reduction and reorganization in business lines which improves the credit risk attached to the outstanding debt, and improves its ability to withstand an economic downturn, CBRS said.

The rating outlook reflects the continuation of buoyant demand for aluminum in the near to medium term while realizing that the pricing downturn may not be over soon because inventories continue to rise and some production capacity remains idle, CBRS said.
